description: EMBOSS 6.6 needleall: the global alignment (Needleman-Wunsch with affine gaps, the program's own scoring: gap of length k costs gapOpen + (k-1)*gapExtend, end gaps free unless endWeight) of every sequence of the set A against every sequence of B, for each B sequence every A sequence, exactly as needle aligns each pair (same rows, ties and single-precision scores). A pair whose score is not above minScore is not reported; the program's error-file line ('Alignment score (S) is less than minimum score(M) for sequences A vs B') is returned in errorText. brief = false adds the Longest_/Shortest_ Identity / Similarity percentages to the sub-header of the formatted output. VERIFICATION: output files (every -aformat) and error files identical to the installed needleall 6.6.0 on 260 / 260 committed random DNA / IUPAC / protein sets (1-3 x 1-4 sequences, every option: matrix, gapOpen, gapExtend, endWeight / endOpen / endExtend, minScore, brief). Use write_alignment (program 'needle') for the EMBOSS output files. Input sequences are read as EMBOSS reads them (A4-3, one shared reader): only letters and '*' are kept; gap characters (- . ~ ?), '#', '+', '_', digits, blanks and every other character are dropped first, and positions, lengths and scores count the cleaned sequence (e.g. needle of AC-GTTAGC.TT* and ACGTTAGCTT: score 58, length 11, as the program).

setA.description: The -asequence set (first member of each pair).

setB.description: The -bsequence sequences (second member of each pair).

namesA.description: Optional names of the A sequences (default a1, a2, ...).

namesB.description: Optional names of the B sequences (default b1, b2, ...).

matrix.description: Optional EMBOSS data matrix (-datafile). Omit for EDNAFULL when every A sequence is nucleotide, EBLOSUM62 otherwise.

minScore.description: -minscore (-10 - 100): minimum score to report an alignment.

brief.description: -brief: false adds the Longest_/Shortest_ Identity / Similarity lines to the sub-header.

sequenceQualifiers.description: EMBOSS sequence-input qualifiers as on the command line, with the input number: -sbegin1 3 -send1 -2 -sreverse1 -slower1 -supper1 -scircular1 -snucleotide1 -sprotein1 and the same with 2 for the second sequence (begin / end: 1-based, negative = from the end; -sreverse: reverse-complement a nucleotide sequence, the range then refers to the original; -snucleotide / -sprotein force the type). Measured on EMBOSS 6.6.0: the alignment covers the range, and the formatted alignment (default format 'pair') reports the positions of the ORIGINAL sequence, counting down for a reversed one. Omit for the whole sequences. The text is resolved exactly as the EMBOSS program resolves it on its command line after the sequence arguments (ACD, 6.6.0): -sbegin1 3, -sbegin1=3, -nosreverse1, -sreverse1 N, any case, -/--/ prefix, and every UNIQUE abbreviation (-sbeg1, -sre2; uniqueness is decided among all qualifiers of the program, an ambiguous or unknown one is refused). The number is the sequence (1, and 2 for the second sequence of a two-sequence program; 1 for a program with one sequence). An unnumbered qualifier belongs to the LAST sequence given (-sbegin 3 is -sbegin2 3 in a two-sequence program) until a qualifier of another sequence ends that tie; after that it applies to all sequences. -sformat selects the file format of the text; -ufo -fformat -fopenfile name the feature file of a program that takes the features of its sequences (diffseq: the files are given by the tool); -sask -squick -sdbname -sid -iquery are accepted without effect (residue strings have no file); any other qualifier or a stray word is refused. Here 1 = the A set, 2 = the B sequences (every member takes the same qualifiers).

alignments.description: Alignments in the program order (for each B sequence every A sequence): names, rows, offsets, score.

errorText.description: The error-file text (pairs not above minScore).

formatted.description: Always null (use write_alignment for the files).

errors.message: a sequence is null or empty
unknown matrix; a penalty or minScore out of range
